nodes.title: R2 · Inaccessible loss: permitted
nodes.labelText: S · A river loss inaccessible to everyone is excluded from that obligation.

nodes.title: KR1 · Rashi: the same verse
nodes.labelText: C · Ordinary return and exceptional acquisition come from one verse, warranting their comparison.

nodes.title: R9 · Supplied: scope of the comparison
nodes.labelTitle: R9 · Supplied: scope of the comparison
nodes.labelText: R · The comparison places ordinary recoverable loss under the prohibition with or without a mark, within that prohibition’s temporal scope.

nodes.title: J1 · Ritva reports: no explicit juxtaposition
nodes.labelTitle: J1 · Ritva reports: no explicit juxtaposition
nodes.labelText: C · The verse does not state the permission alongside the prohibition; it excludes the inaccessible case from the prohibition. Ritva records this objection as coming from Tosafot.

nodes.title: J4 · Tested bridge: transfer every condition
nodes.labelTitle: J4 · Tested bridge: transfer every condition
nodes.labelText: R · Suppose the comparison transfers all awareness and despair conditions unchanged from exceptional permission to ordinary prohibition.

nodes.title: J2 · Ritva reports: unrestricted transfer overreaches
nodes.labelTitle: J2 · Ritva reports: unrestricted transfer overreaches
nodes.labelText: C · If every condition were transferred, ordinary loss would remain prohibited even after actual despair. Ritva records this objection as coming from Tosafot.

nodes.title: J5 · Overextended result (not adopted)
nodes.labelText: R · Ordinary loss would be prohibited even after actual despair. This is the consequence challenged by the reported objection, not Rashi’s qualified conclusion.

nodes.title: J3 · Ritva: prior actual despair can permit
nodes.labelTitle: J3 · Ritva: prior actual despair can permit
nodes.labelText: C · For ordinary loss, actual despair before pickup can permit acquisition, including a marked object whose owner knowingly despairs.

nodes.title: J6 · Ritva: finding immediately after loss
nodes.labelTitle: J6 · Ritva: finding immediately after loss
nodes.labelText: C · Read loss and finding together: the verse addresses a find immediately following the loss, before the owner knows.

nodes.title: J7 · Ritva: only irrecoverability exempted here
nodes.labelTitle: J7 · Ritva: only irrecoverability exempted here
nodes.labelText: C · In that unaware-at-finding case, the verse opens permission only for loss to everyone; the ordinary prohibition also covers unmarked loss.

nodes.title: J8 · Ritva: prior-awareness permission is separate
nodes.labelTitle: J8 · Ritva: prior-awareness permission is separate
nodes.labelText: C · Permission after the owner knows, for an unmarked loss, is derived separately from the garment passage (simlah).

nodes.title: J9 · Ritva: prohibition before awareness
nodes.labelText: C · On this reading, ordinary unmarked loss found before awareness is prohibited; established prior despair remains outside that temporal case.
